prompt: Plan A costs $\$20$ plus $\$5$ per month. Plan B costs $\$10$ plus $\$7$ per month. After how many months do they cost the same?
hint: Write an expression for the cost of each plan after $m$ months. "Cost the same" tells you how to connect them.

hints.text: Write an expression for the cost of each plan after $m$ months. "Cost the same" tells you how to connect them.
Set the costs equal: $20 + 5m = 10 + 7m$. Subtract $5m$ and then $10$ from both sides to get $10 = 2m$.
$10 \div 2 = 5$, so the plans cost the same after $5$ months.

explanation: Plan A costs $20 + 5m$ and Plan B costs $10 + 7m$, so equal cost means $20 + 5m = 10 + 7m$.
Subtract $5m$ from both sides to get $20 = 10 + 2m$, then subtract $10$ to get $10 = 2m$.
Divide by $2$ to get $m = 5$ months. Check: both plans cost $45$ dollars at that point.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: Month 1: A = 25, B = 17. Month 3: A = 35, B = 31. B is catching up by $2 each month.
A starts $10 ahead and B gains $2 per month: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 months to tie.

alternativeExplanations.title: As two racers
steps: Plan A starts 10 dollars ahead but walks 5 per month; B runs 7 per month.
B closes the 10-dollar gap at 2 per month → catches A after 5 months.
